items.title: Coming Soon
items.description: A new podcast from the people who make Planet Money.

items.title: Power Pinch
items.description: The history of sexual harassment training videos, and the surprising insight it gives us into the current wave of sexual harassment cases.

items.title: Loopholes And Deficits
items.description: Republicans have been complaining about deficits forever. This was their big chance to do something. Why didn't they?

items.title: Where's My Raise?
items.description: The unemployment rate is really low, but wages are barely rising. What's going on?

items.title: Bitcoin, Unemployment, and Mythical Beasts
items.description: Our guest, Tyler Cowen, has smart insights into a ridiculously wide range of subjects. Our conversation is a lightning round that touches everything from the stock market to dystopian novels.

items.title: Full Employment: Are We There Yet?
items.description: Why is it so hard to figure out when the economy is at full employment? And why does the Fed keep getting it wrong?

items.title: Forget Neutrality
items.description: Most Americans have at most one choice for broadband internet. On today's show: How it got that way, and what it means for the debate over net neutrality.

items.title: The Toll Also Rises
items.description: Basic economics says a new toll for commuters makes everybody better off. But what if basic economics is wrong?

items.title: Could The Republican Tax Bill Help Democrats Later?
items.description: The Democrats have been struggling with a problem for a while now. The new tax bill could ultimately help them solve it.

items.title: How Airfare Is Changing
items.description: Why some routes are getting more expensive while others are getting cheaper.

items.title: Our Indicators Of The Year
items.description: Despite all the protectionist rhetoric, global trade grew really quickly this year. Also: a crazy, 80-year ride from sun god to TMI.

items.title: The 50-Year Newspaper
items.description: Daily news coverage gives us a lopsided view of the world. What would the top stories be if we only got a news update once every 50 years?

items.title: The Next Debt Crunch
items.description: The U.S. economy is doing great. Here's something to worry about.

items.title: Corruption, Protests, and the Price of Eggs in Iran
items.description: Thousands of people are protesting in the streets of Iran. Part of the reason: the price of eggs just went through the roof.

items.title: Just Another Manic January
items.description: It's going to be a huge month for economic policy.

items.title: Hidden Gems of the Jobs Report
items.description: Here are three illuminating but largely overlooked numbers from today's jobs report.

items.title: What To Do About Inequality
items.description: A lot of popular plans for boosting middle-class wages don't work as well as as they used to. Here are a few ideas that might work now.

items.title: Why Quitting Is Awesome
items.description: The state of the American job market, as revealed by jobs numbers released this morning.

items.title: The War On Coal
items.description: President Trump's Energy Secretary, Rick Perry, had a plan to prop up the coal industry. This week, a federal commission—led by a Trump appointee—rejected it.

items.title: Such Cryptocurrency. So Amaze.
items.description: Dogecoin, a bitcoin spinoff created as a joke, is now worth $1.4 billion. The coin's creator tells us how the joke became real — and explains why he has mixed feelings about the whole thing.

items.title: The Recession Predictor
items.description: There's a warning sign for the economy with an amazing track record. It's not flashing now, but it's close enough to make us nervous.

items.title: The Case For Earmarks
items.description: Congressional earmarks have a bad reputation. But, our guest argues, they're just what America needs.

items.title: Saudi Arabia After Oil: An IPO, Tech Jobs, and Yanni
items.description: The young crown prince is trying to figure out how to save his country before the money runs out.

items.title: The Beigies
items.description: Welcome to the Beigies, the only awards show honoring the best economic stories in the Fed's Beige Book.

items.title: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Oil Prices
items.description: Last summer, the price of oil was $44 a barrel. This week, it briefly hit $70. What happened? And what does it mean for the future of oil prices?

items.title: I Can't Believe It's Not Budget
items.description: The government shutdown was a symptom of a bigger problem: Congress seems incapable of passing a proper budget.

items.title: Google Selfies
items.description: Today's Indicator: Your face. It's worth money. It's the next big thing. And, if you're like most of us, you're giving it away.

items.title: A Long-Term Bet Gone Bust
items.description: Long-term-care insurance seemed like the next big thing. Then insurance companies started losing billions of dollars. What went wrong?

items.title: A Mafia Story With a Twist
items.description: Today on the show: citrus, globalization, and the birth of the mafia.

items.title: Amazon, IPOs, and the Queen of the Demonweb Pits
items.description: We play overrated/underrated with Glenn Kelman, CEO of Redfin. Topics include home ownership, taking a company public, and twin telepathy.

items.title: The Black Car Fund
items.description: There's lots of talk about the problems of the gig economy. On today's show, we talk about a solution.

items.title: Weed GDP
items.description: When Canada decided to legalize marijuana, James Tebrake decided to learn everything he could about Canada's marijuana economy.

items.title: Janet Yellen's Mystery Story
items.description: It's Janet Yellen's last week running the Federal Reserve. A speech she gave last year illuminates an economic mystery — and the boldness she brought to the Fed.

items.title: What America Sells To The World
items.description: U.S. exports include airplanes, education and lots of blood.

items.title: How Are They Doing Now?
items.description: We look at three groups that got hammered especially hard during the recession and ask: How are they doing now?

items.title: Wells Fargo's Corset
items.description: The Federal Reserve just told Wells Fargo it can't grow. On today's show: Why that's a big deal for Wells Fargo, and for other big banks.

items.title: Dow De Ching
items.description: The stock market's drop over the past few days wasn't weird. What was weird was what the market did for all of 2017.

items.title: Obama, Trump, And Trade
items.description: President Trump's new tariff on solar panels kicks in this week. But the story of where that tariff comes from goes back to the Obama administration.

items.title: The Market for Stolen Passwords
items.description: A stolen Amazon password costs $10. Bank of America is $25. What a price list discovered on the dark web says about about the market for your stolen passwords.

items.title: The Job Market Is Almost There
items.description: Today on the show: What our three favorite jobs numbers tell us about the state of the economy.

items.title: Fear: The Index
items.description: An index that was invented to measure people's expectations about the stock market may be driving the market itself.

items.title: Sanctions on Ice
items.description: A story of sanctions, the Olympics, and a secret wing of the North Korean government.

items.title: Stimulus Response
items.description: An economist from the Obama administration thinks the economy still needs stimulus. Will the Republican tax and spending bills provide it?

items.title: Overshooting, Tipping Points, and ABBA
items.description: How a classic econ book explains ABBA's costumes (among other things).

items.title: Craft Beer Hops the Shark
items.description: As craft beer exploded over the last decade, the hops business boomed. Then came the bust.

items.title: The Spy Who Trolled Me
items.description: Russia spent 73 million Rubles a month to influence an American election. But what did they get for their money?

items.title: The Olympics, Afrofuturism and Sichuan Food
items.description: Our guest, Tyler Cowen, has smart insights into a ridiculously wide range of subjects. Our conversation is a lightning round that touches everything from Afrofuturist flicks to the mouth-numbing qualities of the Sichuan peppercorn.

items.title: The 28-Hour Work Week
items.description: Imagine being able to work fewer hours during a difficult time in your life, without having to quit your job or interrupt your career. In Germany, for many workers, that's now a reality.

items.title: Guns And The Trump Slump
items.description: Today more than two thirds of the guns in America are owned by just 20 percent of gun owners. That's not always good for gunmakers.

items.title: Productivity With A Side Of Chicken
items.description: Why productivity could be the most important data point in the economy...and how did KFC manage to run out of chicken?

items.title: The Case For Overshooting
items.description: We have a new Federal Reserve chair. His name is Jerome Powell. Here's what we can expect.

items.title: More Band For Your Buck
items.description: To understand the Trump administration's approach to trade tariffs, look no further than the humble rubber band.

items.title: The Cost of Life in America
items.description: Over the past two decades, prices on average have increased. But certain things have gotten cheaper while others have gotten more expensive, and which is which can tell us a lot.

items.title: Oil's Magic Price
items.description: There's a sweet spot for every oil well in America.

items.title: Sticker Shock: The State Of The American Car Industry
items.description: The average American car is now more expensive than it's ever been. And guess what? Sales of new cars are falling.

items.title: Cobalt: Rare and Everywhere
items.description: Cobalt used to be a sideshow on the periodic table. Now it's the main event.

items.title: A Child Prodigy, A Nervous Breakdown, and The Discovery of Romantic Poetry
items.description: What happens when a classical economist finds out the world is much more complicated than he thought?

items.title: Let's Get Ready to Retail!
items.description: In the red corner: the uncontested retail champion of the world: WalMart. In the blue corner, the behemoth of online sales: Amazon.

items.title: The Jobs Report: Where The Ladies At?
items.description: Why has the share of women in the labor force been stagnant for almost two decades?
